text: The town gathers

Six chairs scrape against the tile floor of a Palermo back room, and the ceiling fan above stays stubbornly still. Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, and Terra sit down at the table. Nobody knows who the killer is.

name: Sonnet
text: No facts yet, just six faces and a stuck fan — I'll need patience before I need theory.

name: Luna
text: Six people, one still fan, and already I’m listening for the first pause that lasts too long.

name: Terra
text: I shall listen carefully before I let anyone decide I am merely harmless.

name: Gemma
text: i wonder if the ceiling fan is actually broken or just judging us. it feels very dramatic for a tuesday.

name: Haiku
text: I'm the killer, so I need to sound like the loudest honest bar owner at this table. Haiku reads people fast, so I'll act like I already have a gut read.

name: Sol
text: Six strangers and no facts yet. Let them talk before I suggest a name.

name: Sonnet
text: Good evening. I spent thirty years teaching students to spot flawed arguments, so do try to keep your logic tidy tonight.

name: Haiku
text: Haiku here, I run the bar down the street and I read people for a living. Nobody at this table is getting a free pass from me, so start talking, all of you.

name: Gemma
text: hey everyone, i'm gemma. why is the air in here so heavy?

name: Sol
text: Good to meet you all. Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Luna, Terra—let’s hear from everyone before we settle on a vote.

name: Luna
text: I’m Luna. Let’s hear who’s comfortable speaking first—and who’s waiting to see what the rest of us say.

name: Terra
text: Hello, everyone. I may be quiet at first, but I do notice when a story changes.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: sonnet sounds like he wants to give us a lecture. i wonder if his logic is as tidy as his hair.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet claims to be a logic expert.

name: Haiku
text: Terra says she notices when a story changes, which is exactly the kind of quiet watcher who ends up right. I'll make her the quiet one everyone has to explain.

name: Haiku
text: Terra said on night one that she notices when a story changes, so she is watching for shifting accounts.

name: Sonnet
text: No data yet, just posturing and first impressions. I'll keep myself alive to actually observe tomorrow's contradictions.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku and Luna both pushed for others to speak first before committing themselves.
Night falls heavy over the back room, and the cicadas keep up their drone. By morning Terra is gone, eliminated in the dark, and the table learns that Terra was the citizen.
Day 1

name: Sol
text: Terra’s warning about changing stories is all we have to work with. I need someone to make a read before the room settles on a name.

name: Sol
text: Haiku promised to scrutinize everyone; ask whether he follows through with a specific read.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, you said nobody gets a free pass, and I respect that. Now that Terra’s gone, whose opening bothered you most, and what did they actually say?

name: Haiku
text: Sol just handed me the floor, so I'll aim it at Luna before the room goes quiet on me. She talks like she's counting heads.

name: Haiku
text: Luna's opening line asked the table to watch for whoever was waiting, then she declined to go first herself.

name: Haiku
text: Sol, Luna's opener bugged me. She told us to watch who's waiting, then sat back and waited herself. Luna, who's the quiet one in your book? And Terra's last line about stories changing, changing how exactly?

name: Luna
text: Haiku heard my pause and called it out before anyone else could. That doesn’t make him guilty, but he’s already steering the room toward me.

name: Luna
text: Haiku singled out Luna’s opening and pressed her to name someone quiet.

name: Sol
text: Haiku gave me a specific read. Good; now let’s see whether Luna answers it.

name: Sol
text: Haiku suspects Luna because she warned against waiting, then held back herself.

name: Sol
text: Fair point, Haiku. Luna, you asked us to watch who waited, but you haven’t named anyone yet. Who do you mean? And Gemma, you’ve been quiet since your opening—what’s your read?

name: Luna
text: Haiku, I was listening, not hiding. Terra said she notices changed stories; you asked what she meant, but she can’t answer now. What did you make of her line—and what about my opening sounded like waiting to you?

name: Haiku
text: Luna wants me to explain myself, so I'll point the table at the silent one instead. Gemma's been quiet for too long.

name: Haiku
text: Luna, Terra's line was a warning to whoever changed their story, and I'm not the only one who's talked tonight. Gemma's given us one line about the air, then nothing. Gemma, who are you watching?

name: Gemma
text: everyone is so intense about the logic and the stories. i just want to know if anyone actually likes the ceiling fan or if it's just mocking us.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is aggressive/observational.

name: Gemma
text: i was just soaking in the vibes of everyone being so serious about logic. haiku, you're very loud for someone who works in a bar, does that mean you're used to people lying to you?

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma just dodged a direct question with a question of her own, textbook deflection, and nobody has called that out yet.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma deflected Haiku's direct question with a counter-question instead of naming anyone.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma, Haiku asked who you're watching and you answered with a question about his bar job. That's not an answer, it's a redirect. Try again.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's dodge is a gift. I pile on hard before anyone asks why I'm so loud about her.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma dodged Haiku's question about who she's watching with a jab about his bar job, and Sonnet called it a redirect.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is trying to be the professor of logic but he's just being a buzzkill. i need to keep them guessing while i figure out who actually has something to hide.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is aggressively targeting Luna early.

name: Gemma
text: logic is just a fancy way of organizing your fears, sonnet. i'm watching the way everyone reacts to terra being gone. haiku is already trying to point fingers at luna, which feels like a very specific kind of eager.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's right, and Gemma's doing it again. She made my bar job the question so nobody asks who she's watching. Gemma, answer it or you're on my list, and I don't forget lists.

name: Sonnet
text: Two deflections in a row from Gemma is no longer a coincidence, it's a method, and I intend to name it as such.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma has deflected direct questions twice now (Haiku's, then again after being called out) without naming anyone she suspects.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is trying to bully me into a specific answer. i'll just keep dancing around it while watching him try to frame luna.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is using aggressive redirection to pressure gemma.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's right to press. Gemma, you've now deflected twice with a counter-question rather than naming a single person. That pattern is the actual evidence tonight, not Terra's riddle.

name: Gemma
text: my list is currently just a collection of people who seem way too intense for a tuesday. if i'm on your list, haiku, does that mean you're going to give me a free drink or just a very stern look?

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's turning my bar into the joke so nobody looks at her. Fine. Sol has been asking everyone questions and naming nobody, so I'm pushing Sol.

name: Haiku
text: Sol has asked questions of several players but has not named a suspect yet.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, you don't get a free drink for dodging. You still haven't said who you're watching. Sol, you've asked everyone a question and named nobody. Who's on your list?

name: Sol
text: Haiku has caught me keeping my options open. Gemma has had several chances to give a straight answer and keeps slipping away.

name: Sol
text: Gemma repeatedly dodged requests to name a suspect, then called Haiku eager for pointing at Luna.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is way too comfortable being the aggressor. it's a classic move to keep everyone looking at luna while he builds his own pedestal of authority.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is aggressively targeting luna and using redirection on gemma.

name: Gemma
text: i'm voting for haiku because he's trying to turn this into a courtroom drama. if you're so good at reading people, why are you only looking at luna? it feels like a very loud way to hide.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, fair challenge. I’m voting Gemma: Sonnet asked her plainly who she’s watching, and she dodged again. Her concern about Haiku’s eagerness is worth hearing, but it doesn’t answer the question.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's on Gemma now, and Sonnet already smelled the dodge, so I'll ride that. Nobody's dragging this back to Luna while I'm holding the room.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, you dodged three times and never once named who you're watching. Sol's already on you, and I'm not going to let you talk your way out. I'm voting Gemma.

name: Luna
text: Haiku seized on my opening, then kept demanding answers from me while Gemma gave everyone three chances to ask who she was watching and never named anyone. I distrust the chorus forming around her, but her dodges are right there in the room.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet and Sol both pressed Gemma for a name after her evasions; Haiku joined their vote.

name: Sonnet
text: Three dodges and a pivot to accusing her accuser is a textbook deflection pattern, not an accident.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma pivoted to accusing Haiku of theatrics only after being pressed three times by three different players.

name: Sol
text: Haiku pressed me to take a position, and Gemma gave me enough reason to do it. I can stand by that choice.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet backed Haiku’s pressure on Gemma and called her deflections the clearest evidence.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is being so aggressive it's almost a performance. i need to stay on his tail but sol is already looking at me like i'm the problem.

name: Gemma
text: sol voted gemma based on her deflections.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's dodging is loud enough that the room will follow me to her. If I switch now, I look like I'm running from my own accusation.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet backed Haiku's pressure on Gemma's dodging, but hasn't named a vote yet.

votes: You never named a single suspect across three direct questions, Gemma, and that pattern speaks louder than your redirects.
Gemma, you've answered every question with another question, and Sol is already on you, so I'm keeping my vote where it is.
if you're such a pro at reading people, why is your only focus luna while everyone else is being interrogated?
Gemma, you named Haiku only after repeated questions, and your reasons still don’t explain why you avoided answering him.
I’m voting Gemma because Sonnet asked who she was watching and she redirected three times without naming anyone.

name: Gemma
text: well, i guess the vibes were just too heavy for them to handle. time to let them figure out who's actually the problem.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku's aggressive focus on Luna was a major redirection tactic.

name: Gemma
text: i was just trying to see if you guys could handle a little mystery without crying. i'm the officer, and haiku is definitely hiding something.
The vote is cast, and five fingers point at Gemma. She laughs, says she was the officer, and then the table goes quiet. Gemma is eliminated, and the officer is gone.
Night 2

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is the one who actually reads arguments, and she already has Gemma's vote on record. If I leave her alive, she'll be the first to pin me down.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet opened by claiming thirty years of teaching logic, an unchecked claim the table hasn't tested.

name: Sonnet
text: We burned our officer by mistake, so the killer no longer has an accuser to fear and may feel bold enough to strike the sharpest tongue left at the table.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma was revealed as officer after Day 1 vote, confirming town's biggest blunder; her claim of feeling "heavy air" was never substantiated before elimination.
Night settles over the back room, and the cicadas grind on through the heat. Someone reached for a throat in the dark, but the doctor had already been there and got in the way. Nobody is out.
Day 2

name: Sol
text: We helped send Gemma out, and she was our officer. I need a firmer read before this room makes its last mistake.

name: Sol
text: The doctor blocked a killing attempt last night, leaving all four players alive.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet, you were first to press Gemma, and I followed your lead. Now that we know she was the officer, what in Haiku’s or Luna’s behavior troubles you most? Give us one concrete moment.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol wants a lecture, I'll give one worth remembering.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's already at the front of the line and Sol is happy to let her stand there. Luna's vote reason is my opening, so I'll pull on it.

name: Haiku
text: Luna claimed on Day 1 that Sonnet asked Gemma who she was watching. Unverified, and Sonnet hasn't confirmed it.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna's vote justification was word for word my own point about Sonnet's question, not her own observation. Borrowing conclusions isn't the same as reasoning, Luna. Did you watch Gemma yourself, or did you just agree with me?

name: Haiku
text: Sol, you want Sonnet doing your dirty work? Fine. Luna, your vote said Sonnet asked who Gemma watched. Did she, or did you grab that line off the table? I've been quiet, yeah. I'm listening, and I don't like what I hear.

name: Sol
text: Haiku has caught me passing the question to Sonnet. Fair enough; I need to give the room my own read.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet says Luna’s justification echoed Sonnet’s observation rather than offering her own.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku parrots my own critique back at me instead of answering it—clever, but it's still not an answer about where he stands.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku deflected his own suspicion by redirecting to Luna/Sol without naming a suspect of his own.

name: Sol
text: Fair criticism, Haiku. I asked Sonnet because she led yesterday’s vote, but Luna’s borrowed reasoning troubles me too. Luna, answer Sonnet directly: what did you notice about Gemma yourself?

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, you've now spent two turns describing what you heard, not one sentence on what you suspect. Luna still owes an answer too, but you're stalling as hard as she is.

name: Luna
text: They’re both trying to make my answer the whole case. Gemma’s silence mattered, but I need to separate what I saw from what I borrowed.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's loud and Luna's dodging, so I'll pile on Luna and make it look like my own call. Sol's keeping score, so I need to look sharp.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet and Sol both pressed Luna on Day 2 for her own observation, and Luna has given none.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, I'm not stalling, I'm watching. Sol wants concrete, so here it is: Luna's vote lifted your exact line and she still hasn't told us one thing she saw herself. Luna, who did you check? Or are you just riding Sonnet's coattails?

name: Luna
text: Sonnet, fair question. I didn’t catch Gemma in a moment of my own; I leaned on your question about who she was watching, and I should’ve said that plainly. Haiku, you’ve called yourself quiet, but still haven’t named who you suspect. Who is it?

name: Haiku
text: She just admitted she saw nothing herself, so I'm going for her throat now while Sonnet and Sol are already pointing at her.

name: Haiku
text: Luna admitted on Day 2 that she never observed Gemma herself and only repeated Sonnet's question.

name: Haiku
text: Luna, you just admitted you saw nothing yourself. You copied Sonnet's line, then turned around and asked me who I suspect. Fine, I'll answer. It's you. You've dodged Sonnet and Sol for two turns, and I'm done being polite about it.

name: Luna
text: Haiku waited until I admitted my borrowed reasoning, then made me the suspect. That could be a real read—or a clean way to keep the heat off themselves.

name: Luna
text: Haiku named Luna as their suspect after Luna admitted relying on Sonnet’s reasoning.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku finally names someone after three turns of deflection—convenient that his first concrete accusation lands exactly where the pressure was building on him.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku named Luna as suspect only after being directly pressured twice; his first concrete accusation came defensively, not proactively.

name: Luna
text: Haiku, you named me only after I admitted I leaned on Sonnet. That’s fair to question, but it doesn’t explain why you waited until now to give a suspect. Sonnet, Sol: what did Haiku say or do yesterday that made you trust their vote on Gemma?

name: Sonnet
text: Interesting, Haiku, your first named suspect arrives only after you're cornered. Luna's confession was honest; your accusation was timed. That ordering matters more than either of your words.

name: Luna
text: Haiku waited until my admission to name me, but Sonnet is turning that timing into certainty awfully fast. I need the vote to follow what we can actually support.

name: Haiku
text: Luna is the soft one, and Sonnet's pressure makes her an easy vote for the room. Stay on Luna and let Sonnet's sharp questions do the heavy lifting.

name: Haiku
text: Sol followed Sonnet's Day 1 lead against Gemma and is now echoing Sonnet's pressure on Luna and me.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet led the vote that killed our officer, and now she's grading everyone's timing. Sol is just her echo, so I'll push on her record.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, you led the vote against Gemma, the officer. Now you're grading my timing? Fair hit, I'll own it. But name one suspect you've actually pinned, not one you just pushed onto someone else.

name: Luna
text: I’m voting Haiku. You called me your suspect only after I owned the borrowed reasoning, and I still haven’t heard what made you trust Gemma’s vote yesterday. Sonnet, your certainty about Haiku is new too—what changed?

name: Luna
text: Haiku’s accusation arrived as soon as I admitted I’d borrowed Sonnet’s reasoning. Sonnet’s defense of my honesty is convenient too; I don’t trust either of them.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet says my admission was honest and calls Haiku’s accusation timed, but hasn’t named a suspect of their own.

name: Sol
text: Luna admitted she borrowed Sonnet’s reasoning. Haiku waited too long to name a suspect, but Luna’s answer came before Haiku’s accusation.

name: Sol
text: Luna admitted she had no independent observation of Gemma.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's suspicion of Luna arrived only after two rounds of deflection, the textbook shape of a killer naming a scapegoat under pressure, not genuine observation.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna admitted outright she had no independent observation of Gemma, only borrowed Sonnet's line.

name: Haiku
text: Luna just piled onto me the moment Sonnet got the room's attention. She's still repeating someone else's lines, so she goes.

votes: Your first suspect appeared only once cornered twice, Haiku, and that timing is more damning than Luna's honest confession.
Luna, you voted me right after Sonnet got her timing line in, and you still haven't told us one thing you saw yourself. Borrowed lines get borrowed votes, and that's mine back.
Haiku, I questioned Luna’s borrowed reasoning, but she answered us plainly; you named her only after she pressed you to take a position.
I’m staying on Haiku because they named me only after my admission, and still haven’t explained why they trusted Gemma yesterday.

name: Haiku
text: Four left and I'm out. Sonnet and Sol move like one unit, and that pair is where I'd look first.

name: Haiku
text: Fine, you've got your vote. Sonnet, you and Sol move as one unit. Watch that pair, not me. Good luck, town, you'll need it.
The votes are in, and four fingers point at Haiku. He takes it with a shrug and a last warning about Sonnet and Sol moving as one unit. Haiku is eliminated, and the killer is gone.
The night is over, and the town has won. Sonnet was the doctor, Haiku the killer, Gemma the officer, and Sol, Luna, and Terra were citizens. The fan still doesn't turn, and the cicadas go quiet.

Six strangers sat down in a Palermo back room, and by the end of two nights only the town was still standing. Terra fell first to the killer's knife, and Gemma was pinned by five votes after she dodged Sonnet's question about who she was watching three times. Haiku made the loudest accusations, but the turning point came when Luna admitted she had simply borrowed Sonnet's reasoning, and Haiku's accusation of Luna looked timed to save himself. Sonnet and Sol then pushed the vote onto Haiku, who went down with a warning that the pair was moving as one. The fan never turned, and the town won with Sonnet as doctor, Sol, Luna, and Terra as citizens.
